lines: Title: Definition of Polynomial from Polynomial Ring over Sequences
Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a [[Definition:Ring with Unity|ring with unity]].
Let $\struct {P \sqbrk R, \oplus, \odot}$ be the [[Definition:Polynomial Ring over Sequences|polynomial ring]] over the [[Definition:Set|set]] of all [[Definition:Sequence|sequences in $R$]]:
where the [[Definition:Operations on Polynomial Ring of Sequences|operations $\oplus$ and $\odot$ on $P \sqbrk R$]] be defined as:
| mr= \sequence {r_0 + s_0, r_1 + s_1, r_2 + s_2, \ldots}
| rc= where $\ds t_i = \sum_{j \mathop + k \mathop = i} r_j \circ s_k$
Let $\struct {R \sqbrk X, +, \circ}$ be the [[Definition:Ring of Polynomials|ring of polynomials over $R$ in $X$]].
Then $\struct {R \sqbrk X, +, \circ}$ and $\struct {P \sqbrk R, \oplus, \odot}$ are [[Definition:Ring Isomorphism|isomorphic]].
Let $P \sqbrk R$ be the [[Definition:Polynomial Ring over Sequences|polynomial ring over $R$]].
Consider the [[Definition:Injection|injection]] $\phi: R \to P \sqbrk R$ defined as:
It is easily checked that $\phi$ is a [[Definition:Ring Monomorphism|ring monomorphism]].
So the set $\set {\sequence {r, 0, 0, \ldots}: r \in R}$ is a [[Definition:Subring|subring]] of $P \sqbrk R$ which is [[Definition:Ring Isomorphism|isomorphic]] to $R$.
Next we note that $P \sqbrk R$ contains the element $\sequence {0, 1, 0, \ldots}$ which we can call $x$.
From the definition of [[Definition:Ring Product|ring product]] on the [[Definition:Polynomial Ring over Sequences|polynomial ring over $R$]], we have that:
{{eqn | r = r_0 \oplus r_1 \circ x \oplus r_2 \circ x^2 \oplus \ldots \oplus r_n \circ x^n
So by construction, $R \sqbrk X$ is seen to be equivalent to $P \sqbrk R$.
It can also be shown that this proof works for the general [[Definition:Ring (Abstract Algebra)|ring]] whether it be a [[Definition:Ring with Unity|ring with unity]] or not.
